queue.opening: Twenty years ago, the last time an unpopular second-term Republican president faced a midterm reckoning, the Democratic Party relied on moderate and even conservative-leaning candidates to reclaim control of Congress. Heath Shuler , the former NFL quarterback, won a North Carolina House seat as a pro-life, pro-gun Democrat. Jim Webb , the former Reagan Navy Secretary and tribune of the Scots-Irish, won a Senate seat in a then–more Republican Virginia. A young politician named Kirsten Gillibrand captured an upstate New York House seat with an “A” rating from the NRA. If the Democrats win the Senate next Tuesday, it will reflect the success of a modified and limited version of that strategy. Yes, the 2026 campaign has featured big progressive bets, like Abdul El-Sayed’s candidacy in Michigan, and big progressive fiascos, like the process that yielded Graham Platner and then Troy Jackson in Maine. But in the end, the expectation that angry Democratic primary voters would turn this into a progressive Tea Party year, with a hyper-ideological cast of candidates, hasn’t matched the reality of the Senate races. Instead, Democrats are competing in swing states and reddish states because they mostly turned to nominees who could present as moderates. queue.dek: The Commerce Department released the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge, which showed inflation trended higher in September, as third-quarter GDP rose more than expected.
queue.opening: The Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge rose further away from the central bank's target in September as consumers face price pressures. The Commerce Department on Thursday reported that the personal consumption expenditures (PCE) index rose 0.5% on a monthly basis in September and was up 3.6% from a year ago. Both figures were in line with the expectations of economists polled by LSEG. Core PCE, which excludes volatile measurements of food and energy prices, was up 0.3% on a monthly basis and 3.1% year over year. Those figures were both in line with economists' expectations. FEDERAL RESERVE MAKES INTEREST RATE DECISION AHEAD OF MIDTERMS Federal Reserve policymakers are focused on the PCE headline figure as they try to bring inflation back to their long-run target of 2%, though they view core data as a better indicator of inflation. Compared with August's readings, headline PCE ticked up from 3.4% to 3.6%, while core PCE rose from 3% to 3.1%. Goods prices were up 3.9% year over year, while services prices increased 3.5% from a year ago in September. The personal savings rate as a percentage of disposable personal income was 3.8%, down from 4% in August. Over the last two years, the savings rate has declined from a peak of 6.2% in April 2025 and from 5.6% in January 2026.
